name: Guava
perishability: Highly perishable. 2–4 days ripe at room temperature; it has the highest post-harvest loss of any fruit studied.
summary: A hardy, cheap 'poor man's apple' that grows across India with two main crops: a rainy-season crop of poorer quality and a prized winter crop, peaking November–February. It bruises and ripens fast, which gives it the highest measured post-harvest loss of any fruit. Pink-fleshed Thai and Taiwan types now command premium prices in cities.
global: India is the largest guava producer. Fresh exports are small; pulp and juice reach the Gulf and Europe.

states.basis: Major producing states (ranked approximately; shares not shown)

belts.name: Prayagraj–Kaushambi
belts.note: Home of Allahabad Safeda, India's best-known guava.

belts.name: Ahilyanagar–Pune
belts.note: Thai and Taiwan pink guava orchards for metros.

seasons.name: Rainy-season crop (ambe bahar)
seasons.note: 'Sow' here means flowering. Insipid fruit, heavy fruit-fly damage; many growers suppress it.

climate.v: 23–28 °C ideal; tolerates heat and drought; young plants suffer in frost.
Cool winters give the best colour and sweetness.
Grows with 1,000 mm or more, but rain at ripening invites fruit fly and anthracnose.
Very adaptable, pH 4.5–8.2; sensitive to waterlogging.

weather_risks.impact: Fruit fly and anthracnose spoil the rainy crop.
Damage to young trees and the winter crop.
Bruised fruit at the end of the winter crop.

pests.name: Fruit flies
pests.impact: The main pest; maggots in rainy-season fruit.

pests.name: Guava wilt
pests.impact: Kills trees; serious in UP and Bihar.

pests.name: Bark-eating caterpillar, mealybug, tea mosquito bug

loss.detail: Farm stage 11.59%, market stage 3.46% — the highest of the fruits studied.

practices: Harvested at colour break; padded crates cut bruising.
Thai and Taiwan types are often bagged on the tree to keep skin clean.
Pulp, jelly, cheese and juice makers use the rainy-season crop.

steps.what: Picked by hand; many orchards are leased to contractors for the season.
Carts and fruit shops; pulp and juice units.

supply_chain.packaging: Crates and baskets; Thai guava in cartons.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Thai / Taiwan pink (e.g. VNR Bihi)
varieties.note: Large fruit, long shelf life, premium in cities.

trade.exports: Small fresh exports; guava pulp and juice to the Gulf and Europe.

policy.what: No MSP; NHB supports high-density orchards.

history.what: Rainy-crop glut of poor fruit; low prices.
Prime winter fruit, especially Allahabad Safeda, sells at a premium.

signals: Winter-crop flowering reports (Jul–Aug) and fruit-fly incidence.
Frost forecasts for UP and MP (Dec–Jan).
business: The highest loss rate of any fruit means cold chain and gentle handling pay back quickly.
Pink Thai guava is a fast-growing premium segment for quick commerce.
Rainy-season fruit is better sent to pulp than to fresh markets.
